Prevention: Control during fallow period by carefully hand picking the weed without breaking the internodes because these can resprout into new weeds.
Destroy either by burying or feeding it to pigs
As seeds can travel on animals and machinery, do not allow animals into an affected area, limit machinery use in the area and keep machinery clean to prevent spread
Plant fragments can travel in soil so clean soil off machinery and tools after use in an infested field
Monitoring: Annual or perennial creeping broadleaved herb.
Stems trailing along the ground, also produces underground stolons.
Leaves dark green, alternate, oval with a pointed tip.
Has small lilac blue flowers; also produces white underground flowers
Early detection and eradication is important, since larger infestations may require herbicide applications
Remove as soon as it is seen in the garden
During the growing season look out for remnants plants around farm, machinery, edges of the fields and pig sty.
This should be done before flowering of the weed
Direct Control: Hand pull remnant plants, taking care not to leave any fragment.
If feasible do this after it has rained (easy to pull); if undertaken during dry spell make sure no fragment remains in the field
Avoid using hand hoe because this will create more weed fragments that will sprout into new weed plants
Stem fragements must dessicate until shrivelled for about a month to prevent resprouting.
Alternatively bury in the ground at least 1 foot deep or feed to livestock
Use conventional tillage as supposed to strip tillage (do not use minimum tillage systems)
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
such as dosage and timing of application.
Apply 2,4D to control young weed plants (3weeks) during fallow.
Salt of 2,4 – dichlorophenoxy (720g per litre of active ingredient per hecatre)
Do not use glyphosate, extreme tolerance reported
